That of the manufacturing workmanship diminishes, perhaps, in all of them without exception.
In consequence of better machinery, of greater dexterity, and of a more proper division and
distribution of work, all of which are the natural effects of improvement, a much smaller
quantity of labor becomes requisite for executing any particular piece of work.
And though, in consequence of the flourishing circumstances of the society, the real price
of labor should rise very considerably, yet the great diminution of the quantity will
generally much more than compensate the greatest rise which can happen in the price.
